lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice talking about fixed and tentative future plans with ska, tänker, and kanske.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Making weekend plans while some details are not decided yet.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Distinguishing a decided plan from a possible plan.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik discuss weekend errands and social plans, separating what is fixed from what is only possible.

main_focus.name: future plans with ska, tänker, and kanske
main_focus.description: Use ska for a planned action, tänker for intention, and kanske for uncertainty.
model_examples: Jag tänker ringa henne, men vi kanske ses senare.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use future plan language naturally 5-6 times, including at least one tentative plan.

avoid_grammar: kommer att as a prediction-focused contrast

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use common weekend-planning chunks and avoid overloading with many future forms.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person asks about weekend plans.
dialogue_shape.middle: They discuss one fixed errand, one intention, and one uncertain social option.
dialogue_shape.ending: They decide what is fixed now and what can be decided later.

target_complexity.repetition: contrast fixed and tentative planning language

sentence_focus: one sentence with ska for a fixed weekend plan
one sentence with tänker for intention
one sentence with kanske for uncertainty
one sentence saying something is not decided yet
one question asking about planned weekend activities
